pass_a_gloss: If then you wish to be caught by the hunters, take care not to make your abode in the valleys, nor to linger anywhere low, but seek the mountains. Go up to the mountain where Jesus was transfigured; go up to the mountain on which, having seen the crowds, he went up, and his disciples followed him, where he opened his mouth and taught, saying: 'Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven,' and the following beatitudes. And it is not possible for these hunters to seize anyone except from the mountains and the hills and the cavities of the rocks. For these three things are said in the prophet: 'I will send many hunters, and they will hunt them upon every mountain and upon every hill and from the cavities of the rocks.' Then how shall I know the rocks and the cavities in the rocks? I come to the Exodus, seeking to find a trace of the account of the cavities of the rocks, and I find Moses there wishing to know God, and God promising him and saying: 'Behold, I will set you in a cleft of the rock, and you shall see my back parts; but my face shall not be seen.' If you perceive there the rock and see there the cleft in the rock, having seen, you perceive God through the cleft of the rock, and you will see also the many rocks and their cavities. Which then is that rock, the one rock? 'But the rock was Christ.' For they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and 'he set my feet upon a rock,' which is said in the ninth and thirtieth Psalm. What is the cleft in the rock? If you perceive the presence of Jesus, having understood him as a rock, you will see the cleft according to his presence, through which cleft the things after God are contemplated. For thus it is contemplated in 'and you will see my back parts.'

pass_b_english: If then you wish to be caught by the hunters, take care not to make your sojourns in the valleys, nor to linger somewhere low, but seek the mountains. Go up to the mountain where Jesus was transformed; go up to the mountain on which Jesus, seeing the crowds, went up, and the disciples followed him, where 'opening his mouth he taught them, saying: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of the heavens,' (Jeremiah 16:16) and the beatitudes that follow these.

And it is not possible for these hunters to catch anyone from elsewhere than from the mountains and the hills and from the clefts of the rocks. For these three things are spoken in the prophet: 'For I will send many hunters, and they will hunt them upon every mountain and upon every hill and from the clefts of the rocks.' (Exodus 33:22–23)

From where then shall I understand the rocks and the clefts in the rocks? I come to Exodus, seeking to find a trace of an account of the clefts of the rocks; I find Moses there wanting to know God, and God promising him and saying: 'Behold, I will set you in a hole of the rock, and you will behold my back parts; but my face will not be seen by you.' (1 Corinthians 10:4) If you understand the rock there and see the hole in the rock, seeing, you look upon God through the hole of the rock, and you will also see the many rocks and their clefts. Which then is that rock—the one rock? 'And the rock was Christ'; for 'they drank from a spiritual rock that followed,' (Psalm 40:2) and 'he set my feet upon a rock' is said in the ninth and thirtieth Psalm. What is the hole in the rock? If you see Jesus’ sojourn, understanding him wholly as rock, you will see the hole according to his sojourn, through which hole the things after God are contemplated. For such a thing is meant in: 'and you will see my back parts.'
